target_symbols: AST node type for method-call (e.g. AST_METHOD_CALL or AST_FIELD_ACCESS dispatch)
new VM opcode (e.g. BC_GET_FIELD or BC_STR_METHOD) and its handler in vm_run
string method dispatch helper(s): length, split, slice, indexOf, replace, startsWith, endsWith, toUpper, toLower, trim
map_find (unchanged but coexists with new dispatch)
TokenType TOKEN_DOT (already present from round 4, reused)
behavior_constraints: `str.length` (property, no parentheses) returns integer character count of the string; `"".length` is 0.
`str.split(delim)` returns an array of strings; when `delim` is empty string, splits into single characters.
`str.slice(start, end)` returns substring from inclusive `start` to exclusive `end`; negative indices not required.
`str.indexOf(sub)` returns first occurrence index or `-1` if not found.
`str.replace(old, new)` replaces only the first occurrence; returns original string unchanged if `old` not found.
`str.trim()` removes leading/trailing ASCII whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines).
All string methods return a new value; the original string is never mutated.
Method calls and property access can be chained (e.g. `s.trim().toLower()`, `"a-b-c".split("-")[1]`).
affected_prior: round 4: hash-map dot access via parse_primary/parse_postfix and BC_HASHMAP_GET — must now type-dispatch instead of unconditionally treating dot as hashmap field.
round 2: array values and `len`/`p` builtins — split() must produce arrays usable by existing array/index machinery.
entities.summary: Add string method-call syntax (`expr.method(args)`) and a `str.length` property by making dot access type-dispatch between hash-map field lookup and built-in string methods/properties, with parser-level recognition of method calls and chaining support.

instruction_head:
Add **method-call syntax** for strings: `expr.method(args)`. Currently, dot access (`obj.field`) only works on hash maps. Extend it so that when the left-hand side is a string, a set of built-in string methods are available. This also means `str.length` (without parentheses) must return the string's character count.

The key challenge is that `obj.field` currently compiles to `BC_HASHMAP_GET`. You must make the runtime (or a new opcode) distinguish between hash-map field access and string method
